entries.defect: The conflict is an ARTEFACT of process parentage, not a real trade-off: the successor already has the information it needs (the in-flight declaration names branch, worktree, pid, log), it lacks only a live process.
The coupling is provably breakable — the detached Sol authoring lane survived a landing, a board rebuild and a failed boundary in the supervising session, measured 13.08.2026.
Delegated AUTHORING runs as a detached process (the author-sol.mjs shape), never as an in-process Agent-tool subagent.
The in-flight declaration becomes the ADOPTION RECORD; what is missing today is that nothing tells the successor the run is now its own.
The handover condition changes from 'no agent in flight' to 'the point I was LANDING is landed'.
The successor must gain a capability it lacks: resume supervision of a process it did not spawn — notice completion without a harness notification, and hand findings back for a second leg.
Failure mode: an adopted run dies unnoticed. The in-flight probe already expires when the work stops moving; expiry must ALERT rather than merely unblock.
Failure mode: two sessions adopt the same run. The batch lock and its fence already serialise ownership.
Failure mode: a detached run outlives its point with nobody landing it. The board now-card and the ETA rule make an unattended run visible to the reader.
Rejected: raising the pool cap. The binding constraint is LANDING throughput (30-90 min per point today), not authoring slots; more authors only queue at the same door.
Rejected: refilling slots to keep the session busy — that is the branch of the dilemma that grows context for no throughput.
Rejected: moving picture judgment or landing out of the main session; they are the serial duties that define it.

The larger driver the problem statement understates: main-session context grows mostly from HARVESTING and BOOKKEEPING (diffs, gates, guard remedies, board), not from spawning — so also split the ROLES into a short-lived dispatcher and a lander, so neither carries the other's history.

Measured by scripts/measure-context-cost.mjs over a full day, in both scopes: median main-session context at handover and the share of spend above 150k context (the 87-94 % figure that motivated the boundary). Success is that figure falling while the number of points landed per day does not.
